messages.subject: Dominant or additive locus
parts:
Dear Karl, 

I would be very grateful if you could help me interpret the results of the estimated effects. 
I worked on an F2 population and detected 4 QTLs for flowering time. 
Here is the result:
Estimated effects:
-----------------
               est       SE       t
Intercept 189.1491   0.2859 661.617
1...@51.4a     1.6292   0.3904   4.173
1...@51.4d     0.9598   0.5286   1.816
3...@67.7a     3.0486   0.4414   6.907
3...@67.7d    -0.2015   0.5432  -0.371
8...@8.9a     -5.2433   0.3940 -13.308
8...@8.9d      1.8724   0.5307   3.528
8...@153.9a    2.4347   0.4352   5.594
8...@153.9d   -0.5190   0.5358  -0.969


the highlighted QTL is the major QTL with LOD score close to 40.

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Dominant or additive locus
parts:
Think of AA, AB, and BB genotypes having average phenotypes -a, +d, and +a, respectively.
For a couple of QTL, (3...@67.7 and 8...@153.9), the estimates are consistent with additive alleles (d could reasonably be 0).
For others, d is bigger than 0 but not quite |a|, so you would maybe say incompletely dominant.

karl
